 * In The High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi

entities.text: High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
the S
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Saurabh Banerjee
 Order

By virtue of the present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), the petitioner, seeks issuance of a writ in the nature of 'Mandamus', directing the respondent to release the petitioner on parole for a period of four weeks or in the alternative direct the respondent to decide the application/
representation dated 06.12.2025 expeditiously.

2. Succinctly put, this Court vide order dated 27.11.2025 in CRL.A. 1060/2018 dismissed the appeal preferred by the petitioner thereby upholding the judgement on conviction dated 29.05.2018 as well as order on sentence dated 03.07.2018 passed by the learned Trial Court arising out of FIR No.75/2015 registered at PS: Timarpur, Delhi, under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act)

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 30/03/2026 at 21:59:31 and Sections 376(2)(f),(i),(j),(n)/506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC), whereby the petitioner was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten years along with fine of Rs.5000/- and in default thereof, to undergo simple imprisonment for six months for the offence punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act; to undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years along with fine of Rs.2000/- and in default thereof, simple imprisonment for two months for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(f)(i)(n) of the IPC; and simple imprisonment for two months for offence punishable under Section 506 of the IPC.
3.

Since the petitioner was aggrieved by the dismissal order dated 27.11.2025 in CRL.A.1060/2018 passed by this Court, an application/ representation dated 06.12.2025, was made before the Competent Authority seeking grant of parole for filing a SLP before the Hon'ble Supreme Court against the order dated 27.11.2025, dispatched on 15.12.2025, which has yet not been decided upon V vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66391316/
1 within the period of four weeks, in terms of the Rule 1217 of the Delhi Prison Rules, 2018 (Rules).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Issue notice.
Learned ASC for the State accepts notice.

5. At the outset, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner intends to file an SLP before the Hon'ble Supreme Court so as to avail his remedy enshrined under Article 22(1) of the Constitution of India, as also to maintain social-ties with society and reconnect with his family members.

Although, the petitioner had initially made an application before the Competent Authority for grant of parole for a period of four weeks, however, as the same is yet to be decided in compliance of the This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 30/03/2026 at 21:59:31 aforesaid rules, the petitioner has filed the present petition before this Court.
6. Further, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has spent over a period of four years and three months in prison, and his conduct while in custody has been satisfactory.

Further, since the delay by the Competent Authority in rendering its decision has already caused grave prejudice to the petitioner, the present petition be allowed and the petitioner be released on parole to pursue his remedies, before the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
7. Learned ASC for the State, submits that the application/ representation dated 06.12.2025 is pending before the Competent Authority and the same will be decided soon.

8. Though the same reliefs have been granted to various inmates under similar circumstances by this Court in W.P.(CRL) 224/2026 vide order dated 19.02.2026, however since the representation dated 06.12.2025 has not been decided yet, the Competent Authority is requested to decide the application/ representation dated 06.12.2025 within a period of two weeks.

9. Accordingly, the present petition is allowed and disposed of.
SAURABH BANERJEE, J MARCH 27, 2026/Ab
